title: Layer, blend, then lift
goal: Soften transitions without muddying the lights.
kit: HB, 2B, 4B; clean stump or folded tissue; kneaded eraser.

steps.title: Compare three treatments
steps.text: Look for the difference between visible strokes, softened tone and a lifted light. Blending changes edges and texture; it does not replace a sound value map.
steps.talk: Compare three treatments. Look for the difference between visible strokes, softened tone and a lifted light. Blending changes edges and texture; it does not replace a sound value map. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Can you identify where the light should remain?
steps.check: Can you identify where the light should remain?

steps.title: Light construction
steps.text: Draw three simple ovals. Reserve a small upper-left light in each. Use your palest construction lines.
steps.talk: Light construction. Draw three simple ovals. Reserve a small upper-left light in each. Use your palest construction lines. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are the reserved lights in the same position?
steps.check: Are the reserved lights in the same position?

steps.title: Map three values
steps.text: Assign a light, middle and dark to each oval. Keep their relative positions consistent with upper-left lighting.
steps.talk: Map three values. Assign a light, middle and dark to each oval. Keep their relative positions consistent with upper-left lighting. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are the darks opposite the light?
steps.check: Are the darks opposite the light?

steps.title: Add transitional values
steps.text: Insert a halftone between light and middle, then a darker halftone before the shadow. Layer gradually.
steps.talk: Add transitional values. Insert a halftone between light and middle, then a darker halftone before the shadow. Layer gradually. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Do transitions have enough space to turn?
steps.check: Do transitions have enough space to turn?

steps.title: Layer first
steps.text: Fill gaps with overlapping strokes. Deepen only the shadow. Leave the first oval visibly hatched for comparison.
steps.talk: Layer first. Fill gaps with overlapping strokes. Deepen only the shadow. Leave the first oval visibly hatched for comparison. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Is there already a readable form before blending?
steps.check: Is there already a readable form before blending?

steps.title: Blend selectively
steps.text: Use a clean tool on the second oval, moving from lighter to darker areas. Use a fresh surface for the light. Avoid fingers, which can transfer oils.
steps.talk: Blend selectively. Use a clean tool on the second oval, moving from lighter to darker areas. Use a fresh surface for the light. Avoid fingers, which can transfer oils. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Have you preserved the main value separation?
steps.check: Have you preserved the main value separation?

steps.title: Lift the light
steps.text: Dab a light into the third oval. Build it gradually rather than scrubbing a white hole. Some graphite may not lift completely.
steps.talk: Lift the light. Dab a light into the third oval. Build it gradually rather than scrubbing a white hole. Some graphite may not lift completely. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Does the highlight have a controlled edge?
steps.check: Does the highlight have a controlled edge?

steps.title: Restore dark accents
steps.text: Reinforce a small shadow area softened by blending. Avoid outlining the whole object.
steps.talk: Restore dark accents. Reinforce a small shadow area softened by blending. Avoid outlining the whole object. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are the darkest accents limited?

steps.title: Compare and repeat
steps.text: Write one benefit and one drawback of blending your paper. Repeat a small oval with half as much blending.
steps.talk: Compare and repeat. Write one benefit and one drawback of blending your paper. Repeat a small oval with half as much blending. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Which version describes the form more clearly?
steps.check: Which version describes the form more clearly?

source: Original procedural instructional study; no external reference photograph.
drill: Repeat the study at half size without the grid. Compare your darkest dark, lightest light and largest shape before adding detail.
